candidates.source_name: Athanasius of Alexandria / Orationes contra Arianos III.30
candidates.source_attribution: Athanasius of Alexandria, Orationes contra Arianos (Four Discourses Against the Arians, I-IV), in Select Writings and Letters of Athanasius, Nicene and Post-Nicene Fathers (NPNF), Series 2, Vol. 4, ed. Archibald Robertson (Oxford / T&T Clark, 1892). PD. Greek text in Migne PG 26 (1857).
candidates.draft_body:
Athanasius of Alexandria Orationes contra Arianos III.30 (c. 350 AD)

'Jesus said unto them, Verily, verily, I say unto you, Before Abraham was, I am' — Athanasius marks prin Abraam genesthai egō eimi (before Abraham came-to-be, I AM) as Christ's DIRECT ARTICULATION OF THE DIVINE NAME (Exo 3:14 egō eimi ho ōn). The tense-juxtaposition is crucial: Abraham came-to-be (genesthai, aorist-of-becoming, creaturely-temporality) versus I AM (eimi, present-of-eternal-being, divine-timelessness). The Word's pre-Abrahamic-existence is not 'older-than-Abraham' (which would be creaturely-comparative) but in-a-different-tense entirely — eternal-being-versus-temporal-becoming. The Jewish-interlocutors recognize the blasphemy-claim and pick up stones to kill him (Jn 8:59), confirming they-understood the egō-eimi as divine-self-identification.
candidates.reviewer_notes: Curated PD interpretive summary representing the Ethiopian Tewahedo tradition's reading via Athanasius of Alexandria, Orationes contra Arianos III.30. 'Jesus said unto them, Verily, verily, I say unto you, Before Abraham was, I am' — Athanasius marks prin Abraam genesthai egō eimi (before Abraham came-to-be, I AM) as Christ's DIRECT ARTICULATION OF THE DIVINE NAME (Exo 3:14 egō eimi ho ōn). The tense-juxtaposition is crucial: Abraham came-to-be (genesthai, aorist-of-becoming, creaturely-temporality) versus I AM (eimi, present-of-eternal-being, divine-timelessness). The Word's pre-Abrahamic-existence is not 'older-than-Abraham' (which would be creaturely-comparative) but in-a-different-tense entirely — eternal-being-versus-temporal-becoming. The Jewish-interlocutors recognize the blasphemy-claim and pick up stones to kill him (Jn 8:59), confirming they-understood the egō-eimi as divine-self-identification.
